title: Qman DirectPath supported qualification catalog
x-qmanInteroperableIntegerRange: Every JSON numeric integer is in -9007199254740991..9007199254740991 before canonicalization; wider values use schema-defined decimal strings.

revocationBehavior.description: Catalog-wide profile-withdrawal behavior projected into every supported QualificationProfile. Each deny/revocation entry independently carries its selector-specific behavior.

x-qmanRevocationRule: revocationBehavior is the catalog-wide profile-withdrawal behavior projected into every supported QualificationProfile. Each denyAndRevocationEntries[].revocationBehavior is selector-specific and applies only when that entry's selector matches; it does not override the catalog-wide profile field. A revoked/absent record denies every new power-on, reservation, and relocation. DENY_NEW_AND_NEXT_POWER_ON maps to NORMAL: an already attached VM may run until its next explicit power transition. DENY_NEW_AND_REQUIRE_CONTROLLED_STOP maps to CRITICAL: the controller creates an explicit, auditable stop-maintenance intent and performs normal stop/release; it never silently kills a VM or force-frees a lease. Failure to prove clean release quarantines the complete scope.
x-qmanSignatureRule: Set catalogDigest and signature to null, canonicalize the complete object, hash into catalogDigest, and sign ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/SUPPORTED-CATALOG/V1) || 0x00 || the canonical bytes with a PRODUCT_RELEASE key. The candidate catalog contains no receipt/hash of the external anchor that accepts it. After signature/chain validation, independently supplied monotonic catalog-anchor state must accept catalogSequence/catalogDigest and is advanced in a separate CAS, preventing catalogDigest↔anchorDigest fixed points.
